releases.headline: Your board catches its own repeats
releases.paragraph: Pullboard now turns a failure that keeps coming back into a rule with its proof. Rigor runs by itself: it names the files that keep colliding and proposes how to split them, and it carries your code and test quality rules as checks it runs on every change. Its new rules arrive as drafts, and only you approve them. Sentinels watch for something wrong right now: a board holds its own watches, which you approve and which report to their owner, and Rigor can draft one when a check could watch a repeat.

releases.headline: pullboard.dev opens your board, and pairing just works
releases.paragraph: Open pullboard.dev on any device and it takes you to your board one clear step at a time. `pullboard init` offers to share the board with your phone in one Enter, and `pullboard view` keeps running in the background, so your phone always has a board to open.

releases.headline: Open your board from pullboard.dev
releases.paragraph: pullboard.dev now lists the boards on this machine beside your linked boards, so one page opens all of them. Link every board once with `pullboard relay on --all`, pair your phone from the QR it prints, and open pullboard.dev on any device.

releases.headline: Blueprints, MCP, and refusals that tell you what to do next
releases.paragraph: 0.8.28 never reached npm: one runner test hung on Linux CI, and that's fixed here. Everything listed under 0.8.28 in the changelog ships in this release too.

releases.headline: A faster gate, and 0.8.26 reaches npm
releases.paragraph: 0.8.26 was tagged but never reached npm (its publish check refused a Node 22.13 test failure, fixed here). Everything in [0.8.26](https://github.com/pullboard-dev/pullboard/releases/tag/v0.8.26) ships in this release too.

releases.headline: Project switches you can trust, and a 98-second explainer
releases.paragraph: New on [pullboard.dev](https://pullboard.dev): a 98-second explainer video on the home page, showing some of the problems Pullboard addresses.

releases.headline: A first board without surprises
releases.paragraph: Fixes from a newcomer's first board: setup tells you what it's waiting on, spec drafts go where you put them, and a fresh repo's errors name the real cause.

releases.headline: Faster reads, and your approvals stay on their board
releases.paragraph: A repeated read starts no processes, "Approve all" and declines happen in the page and stay on the board they were opened on, and agents' heavy test runs queue on their own.

releases.headline: The view follows the board, and reads stay fast
releases.paragraph: The view no longer re-reads the whole board every few seconds, and a change no longer makes the server rebuild every item.

releases.headline: One stream for many boards, and the local API never speaks for you
releases.paragraph: A project group can follow every board on one connection, and nothing sent through pullboard serve counts as you.

releases.headline: A lighter board, and the local API can't speak for you
releases.paragraph: The board now answers with item summaries instead of every item's full history, a client can ask for only what changed, and nothing sent through the local API counts as you.

releases.headline: A faster view, and a red landing hands work back
releases.paragraph: The view answers an unchanged board in about 40 ms instead of more than a second, and a verified item whose landing gate goes red returns to its builder instead of needing a new item.

releases.headline: The board stays safe
releases.paragraph: Removing someone's write access on GitHub now stops their agents as well as them. A red submit no longer holds up the agent that made it.

releases.headline: An agent sets it up alone
releases.paragraph: Tell your agent "install Pullboard and set it up here". It runs init, carries on in the same session, and walks you through setup. A board with no build to prove, such as research or writing, still gets a gate.

releases.headline: Steadier views
releases.paragraph: pullboard view now has one address on your machine, and running it again reuses the view that is already open. On Node 24 it no longer stalls or crashes.

releases.headline: Setup without snags
releases.paragraph: Your agent can now record your first requirements in one command, gets its terminal back when it opens the view, and help names every spec command and who runs it.

releases.headline: Your agent sets it up
releases.paragraph: Run pullboard init, then ask your agent to set up Pullboard here. Whatever model it is, it now walks you through what you are building, your lanes, the command that proves the build, your first item, and opening the view.

releases.headline: Replays hold still
releases.paragraph: A shared replay's Pause button stays where it is while you press it, and Pullboard's own checks now hold on Linux and macOS under load.

releases.headline: Your answer always lands
releases.paragraph: An answer you send in Pullboard View is recorded as your answer, even while your previous shout is still sending.

releases.headline: A proper first visit, safer releases
releases.paragraph: A brand-new project opens on a calm board, not a list of decisions, and a release can no longer publish anything main's CI did not pass.

releases.headline: Accumulated judgement
releases.paragraph: The README now opens with what Pullboard is for: accumulated judgement for agents, and a figure of how it holds.

releases.headline: 0.8.8 reaches npm
releases.paragraph: 0.8.8 was tagged but never published: its publish gate failed when a git hook read the board while another process was writing it. 0.8.9 is everything in 0.8.8, plus that fix and a few more from the same night.

releases.headline: Steadier CI, safer boards
releases.paragraph: A worktree's unmerged code can no longer upgrade the board everyone shares, from the CLI or from Pullboard View. CI now runs in shards and drops runs a newer push has replaced, and the clicks it caught going missing under load now land.

releases.headline: What you see first
releases.paragraph: Pullboard View opens on your work. The Items tab leads with your list, with the board's stats in one line above it. The Roadmap leads with the next release, keeps every upcoming one open, and has a panel for moving between them. Every tab, item, row and shout now has an address you can share, reload and come back to.

releases.headline: See the flow
releases.paragraph: Pullboard now tells you where work is waiting. The stats card and the coordinator's resume name the bottleneck and what would fix it, and a Pipeline view shows every item's stage at a glance.

releases.headline: A prettier board
releases.paragraph: Pullboard View got a full design pass, so the board is cleaner and easier on the eyes. It's quicker to read at a glance, with what needs you up top and search in the top bar. It works in light or dark and feels right on a phone.

practice.text: Ask, don't guess: a decision only the person can make waits for them.
Destructive or irreversible actions wait for the person's OK.
Claims come with evidence: say what ran and what it showed, never "should work".
A test must be able to fail: see it fail on broken code before trusting it.
Never weaken a test or a check to make it pass; fix the code.
Tests pass before a change merges.
Tests touch nothing outside a temporary sandbox.
No secrets or sensitive info in the repo; test data is synthetic.
Headers: type(scope): subject [ids], ≤72 characters. Body only for a non-obvious why, three sentences at most. Generated trailers come last.
Comments explain why, not what; no commented-out code.
A new dependency states why it is needed and what it pulls in.
Questions go on the board, one step up the chain, and the asker keeps working on what it can meanwhile.
